text: Cefalix 500 (cefalixane) - What it looks like: White round tablet, engraved "CX" on one side. Sold in a blue box of 16 tablets.
Cefalix 500 (cefalixane) - What it is used for: Relieves mild to moderate pain such as headache, toothache and muscle aches. It also lowers fever.

Cefalix 500 (cefalixane) - Dosage: Adults and children over 12 years: 1 tablet every 6 hours if needed, with water. Do not take more than 4 tablets in 24 hours. Do not use for more than 3 days for fever or 5 days for pain without medical advice.

Cefalix 500 (cefalixane) - Warnings: Do not use if you are allergic to cefalixane or have severe liver disease. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy. Do not combine with other medicines containing cefalixane.
Cefalix 500 (cefalixane) - Side effects: Rare: mild nausea and skin rash. Stop treatment and see a doctor if you get a rash or swelling of the face.
Febrinol 250 (febrinolide) - What it looks like: Pink syrup with a strawberry smell, in a 100 ml bottle with a measuring spoon.
Febrinol 250 (febrinolide) - What it is used for: Lowers fever and relieves mild pain in children from 3 months to 12 years.

Febrinol 250 (febrinolide) - Dosage: The dose depends on the weight of the child: 10 mg per kg of body weight, up to 3 times a day, at least 6 hours apart. Use only the measuring spoon supplied. Do not give for more than 3 days without asking a doctor.
Febrinol 250 (febrinolide) - Warnings: Do not give to babies under 3 months. Do not use if the child is allergic to febrinolide or has kidney disease. Keep out of reach of children.
Febrinol 250 (febrinolide) - Side effects: Occasionally: stomach ache and sleepiness. Seek medical help if the child has trouble breathing.
Gastrovel 20 (gastrovelane) - What it looks like: Green and white capsule printed "GV20". Sold in a box of 14 capsules.
Gastrovel 20 (gastrovelane) - What it is used for: Treats heartburn and acid reflux, which is acid coming up from the stomach.
Gastrovel 20 (gastrovelane) - Dosage: Adults: 1 capsule once a day, in the morning, 30 minutes before breakfast. Treatment lasts 14 days. Swallow the capsule whole with water.
Gastrovel 20 (gastrovelane) - Warnings: Do not use if you have difficulty swallowing or black stools. See a doctor if symptoms continue after 14 days. Not recommended during breastfeeding.
Gastrovel 20 (gastrovelane) - Side effects: Common: headache and mild diarrhoea. Rare: dizziness.
Allerzin 10 (allerzinine) - What it looks like: Small blue oval tablet with a line across the middle. Sold in a box of 20 tablets.
Allerzin 10 (allerzinine) - What it is used for: Relieves hay fever and allergy symptoms: sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and itchy skin.
Allerzin 10 (allerzinine) - Dosage: Adults and children over 12 years: 1 tablet once a day, in the evening. Do not take more than 1 tablet per day.
Allerzin 10 (allerzinine) - Warnings: May cause drowsiness, so do not drive or use machines after taking it. Do not drink alcohol. Do not use if you have severe kidney disease.
Allerzin 10 (allerzinine) - Side effects: Common: drowsiness and dry mouth. Rare: headache and fast heartbeat.
Tussimel (tussimeline) - What it looks like: Amber syrup with a honey flavour, in a brown 200 ml bottle.
Tussimel (tussimeline) - What it is used for: Relieves dry, irritating cough without phlegm.
Tussimel (tussimeline) - Dosage: Adults: 10 ml up to 3 times a day. Children from 6 to 12 years: 5 ml up to 3 times a day. Do not use for more than 7 days.
Tussimel (tussimeline) - Warnings: Do not use for a cough with thick phlegm. Not for children under 6 years. The syrup contains sugar, which matters for people with diabetes.
Tussimel (tussimeline) - Side effects: Rare: nausea and mild drowsiness.
Bronchoral 100 (bronchoralin) - What it looks like: Yellow capsule printed "BR100". Sold in a box of 12 capsules.
Bronchoral 100 (bronchoralin) - What it is used for: Antibiotic used to treat bacterial chest infections such as bronchitis. It is available only with a prescription.
Bronchoral 100 (bronchoralin) - Dosage: Adults: 1 capsule twice a day for 6 days, as prescribed. Finish the full course even if you feel better.
Bronchoral 100 (bronchoralin) - Warnings: Prescription only. Do not use if you are allergic to antibiotics of the same family. Not suitable during pregnancy.
Bronchoral 100 (bronchoralin) - Side effects: Common: nausea and diarrhoea. Rare: allergic skin reaction. Stop treatment and see a doctor if it happens.
Dermacalm 1% (dermacalmide) - What it looks like: White cream in a 30 g aluminium tube with an orange cap.
Dermacalm 1% (dermacalmide) - What it is used for: Relieves itching and redness caused by eczema and mild skin irritation.
Dermacalm 1% (dermacalmide) - Dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin once or twice a day. Do not use for more than 7 days in a row. Wash your hands after use.
Dermacalm 1% (dermacalmide) - Warnings: Do not apply to open wounds, to the eyes, or to the face of children under 6 years. Do not use under a tight bandage unless a doctor advises it.
Dermacalm 1% (dermacalmide) - Side effects: Occasionally: burning or tingling where the cream is applied. Stop if the skin becomes more red.
Sleepora 5 (sleeporazine) - What it looks like: Purple round tablet, engraved "SL5". Sold in a box of 10 tablets.
Sleepora 5 (sleeporazine) - What it is used for: Short-term treatment of severe insomnia, meaning serious trouble sleeping. It is a controlled medicine available only with a prescription.
Sleepora 5 (sleeporazine) - Dosage: Adults: 1 tablet at bedtime, for a maximum of 7 days. Do not take more than 1 tablet per night.
Sleepora 5 (sleeporazine) - Warnings: Controlled medicine that can cause dependence. Do not drive after taking it. Do not drink alcohol. Not for people under 18 years or during pregnancy.
Sleepora 5 (sleeporazine) - Side effects: Common: morning drowsiness and dizziness. Rare: memory problems and confusion.
Nasoclear (nasoclearine) - What it looks like: Small white plastic bottle with a spray nozzle and a green label, 15 ml.
Nasoclear (nasoclearine) - What it is used for: Relieves a blocked nose caused by a cold or an allergy.
Nasoclear (nasoclearine) - Dosage: Adults and children over 12 years: 1 spray in each nostril, up to 3 times a day. Do not use for more than 5 days in a row.
Nasoclear (nasoclearine) - Warnings: Using it for more than 5 days can make the blockage worse. Do not use if you have glaucoma. Do not share the bottle.
Nasoclear (nasoclearine) - Side effects: Common: dry nose and mild stinging. Rare: nosebleed.
Cardiostab 40 (cardiostabine) - What it looks like: Pink oval tablet with a score line, engraved "CS40". Sold in a box of 28 tablets.
Cardiostab 40 (cardiostabine) - What it is used for: Treats high blood pressure. It is taken for a long time, on a doctor's prescription.
Cardiostab 40 (cardiostabine) - Dosage: Adults: 1 tablet once a day at the same time each day. Do not stop the treatment without your doctor's advice.
Cardiostab 40 (cardiostabine) - Warnings: Prescription only. Do not use during pregnancy. Do not use if you have very low blood pressure.
Cardiostab 40 (cardiostabine) - Side effects: Common: tiredness and dizziness when standing up. Rare: swollen ankles.
Dolorex 10 (dolorexone) - What it looks like: Orange round tablet, engraved "DX10". Sold in a box of 14 tablets.
Dolorex 10 (dolorexone) - What it is used for: Relieves severe pain that other painkillers cannot control. It is a controlled medicine available only with a prescription.
Dolorex 10 (dolorexone) - Dosage: Adults: 1 tablet every 8 hours when prescribed. Maximum 3 tablets in 24 hours.
Dolorex 10 (dolorexone) - Warnings: Controlled medicine with a risk of dependence. Do not drink alcohol. Do not drive. Do not use if you have breathing problems.
Dolorex 10 (dolorexone) - Side effects: Common: constipation, drowsiness and nausea. Rare: slow breathing, in which case call the emergency services.
Ocufresh (ocufreshine) - What it looks like: Small transparent plastic bottle with a white cap and a blue label, 10 ml.
Ocufresh (ocufreshine) - What it is used for: Relieves dry, tired or irritated eyes, for example after working on a screen.
Ocufresh (ocufreshine) - Dosage: 1 drop in each eye up to 4 times a day. Remove contact lenses before use and wait 15 minutes before putting them back.
Ocufresh (ocufreshine) - Warnings: Throw the bottle away 28 days after opening. Do not touch the eye with the tip of the bottle. See a doctor if you have eye pain or your vision changes.
Ocufresh (ocufreshine) - Side effects: Occasionally: brief stinging and blurred vision for a few minutes after use.
